I farm 10.1 mu, and with only two people in the household and some off-farm work, I will keep the plan simple and familiar. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to use my well irrigation, spread labor across the year, and protect grain output. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I have long experience with it, but cotton takes more field management and more pesticide work, so I will not expand it. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stand establishment, because after 40 years farming I care most about stable output and avoiding replanting trouble. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive rates, because I want dependable yield without wasting money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize and cotton because wheat in my area usually responds clearly to water, especially at key stages. I will keep rotary tillage for most fields because it saves labor and matches my scale. My goal this year is stable production, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
